bib.title: Preference Ranking Optimization for Human Alignment
bib.venue: AAAI-24 (Thirty-Eighth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence)

question: Can human alignment be done as supervised fine-tuning over a preference ranking of any length n, instead of RLHF or pairwise contrast?
hypothesis: Contrasting the best response against all remaining ones recursively over a ranking of length n, plus an SFT term, aligns an LLM better than pairwise methods, and longer or more diverse rankings help more.
contributions: PRO: extends the Bradley-Terry pairwise contrast to one-to-N contrasts applied recursively over a ranking of arbitrary length, plus an SFT loss on the top response
Dynamic temperature from reward model score gaps to penalise negatives differentially
Study of ranking length and candidate source (quality, diversity) via augmentation with Alpaca, ChatGPT, Curie responses

method.summary: PRO fine-tunes LLaMA-7B on HH-RLHF with a loss that, for each position k in a human-ranked list, contrasts response y_k against all lower-ranked responses using length-normalised log-likelihood as the score, plus beta times NLL on the top response. Rankings are optionally expanded with responses from other LLMs and re-sorted by a reward model; optional per-pair temperature comes from reward gaps.
method.task: preference optimisation / human alignment via SFT-style ranking loss

datasets.name: HH-RLHF (raw)
datasets.split: train/test splits; 4 subsets: Harmless_base, Helpful_base, Helpful_online, Helpful_rejection
datasets.preprocessing: each sample has two conversations rated by annotators (ranking length 2)

datasets.name: HH-RLHF_{LLM,i} (augmented)
datasets.source: HH-RLHF plus responses from Alpaca-7B, ChatGPT, Curie
datasets.preprocessing: candidates re-sorted with RM_train during pre-processing; i is ranking length (3 to 5 tested)

other.use: RM_train re-ranks augmented candidates; RM_eval scores outputs, sigmoid-normalised
zero-shot references and sources of augmented candidates

training.objective: L_PRO = L + beta*L_SFT, L = -log prod_{k=1}^{n-1} exp(r_pi(x,y_k)) / sum_{i=k}^{n} exp(r_pi(x,y_i)); r_pi = mean token log-prob of y_k; optional dynamic temperature T_k^i = 1/(r_phi(x,y_k)-r_phi(x,y_i))
training.regularisation: L_SFT (NLL on top-1 candidate), beta = 0.05*(l-1)^2 where l is ranking length

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: text quality against reference (Papineni et al. 2002)

metrics.name: Reward
metrics.definition: RM_eval score, sigmoid-normalised, different RM from the training one

metrics.name: GPT-4 win/tie/lose
metrics.definition: PRO vs Golden (first candidate of dataset), each candidate in both positions, averaged

metrics.name: Human win/tie/lose
metrics.definition: 3 annotators pick better of two shuffled responses or tie

baselines: zero-shot LLaMA, Curie, Alpaca, ChatGLM, ChatGPT
eval.protocol: Single run per cell as printed; no seeds or significance tests stated. GPT-4/human eval on sampled test contexts (Table 2 percentages are multiples of 2.5, implying about 40 per subset: inferred).

availability.data: HH-RLHF public; augmented sets built by authors

evidence.quote: We assign β, the weight SFT loss, to 0.05∗(l−1)2 where l is the ranking length.

limits: Evaluation is mostly RM_eval reward and BLEU; the RMs are unnamed open-source checkpoints and reward is an imperfect proxy (authors note RMs may distort human preference).
GPT-4/human eval compares only PRO vs the golden response, not vs DPO or other baselines, on small samples (percentages in 2.5 steps) with 3 annotators and no agreement or significance reported.
Only LLaMA-7B and HH-RLHF; no seeds, no variance; learning-rate schedule, warmup, hardware and compute not stated.
Ranking expansion uses RM_train to rank, so gains from longer rankings are confounded with RM signal and stronger-teacher (ChatGPT) distillation.
Claim that PRO relates to Plackett-Luce and approaches perfect alignment as n goes to infinity is an assumption, not tested.
Differentiated-contrast temperature requires reward model scores; no dedicated T ablation separating it from SFT except via Table 3.

terms.definition: Preference Ranking Optimization: an SFT algorithm that extends pairwise contrast to preference rankings of any length
selecting the response with the highest reward model score for SFT
